excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past six months, the "lobster fever" sparked by OpenClaw has plunged the AI community into collective euphoria: AI writes code for you, replies to emails, and even takes over devices, as if the countdown to "replacing humans" has already begun. Nvidia's Jensen Huang called it "one of the most important software releases ever," adding fuel to the frenzy. But as the bubble slightly deflates, the IoT industry is left with awkward cracks on the beach. An accidental email deletion in a company's lab, a source code leak at another firm, and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's March advisory on preventing security risks from OpenClaw ("Lobster") open-source intelligent agents all remind us: when general-purpose agents pursue "omniscience and omnipotence," they often come with the risk of losing control. For IoT developers, the reality is even harsher—private protocols pile up, documentation is incomplete, and even if AI can write functional code in 15 minutes, the tedious testing and release processes can still stretch delivery cycles to days. This clarity stems from a deep insight into the industry. The current IoT sector doesn't need a vague "digital god," but a truly usable and effective engineering system. items.title: StackScope – I crawled over 40k indie launches to see what they ship
items.raw_excerpt: Hey all, I built StackScope, a crawler/catalogue that looks at new product launches and shows what they were built with. It watches launches from Product Hunt, Show HN, and PeerPush, then crawls the public site behind each one. The goal is to show what people actually launched with: hosting, frameworks, analytics, DNS, security headers, legal pages, AI-builder signals, and other public clues. I started building it because most stack-detection sites look at the web as a whole. I was more interested in the current indie launch scene: what people are choosing right now, at the point they first put something in public. A few implementation details: it runs on .NET, uses Playwright for rendered pages, and has a first-party fingerprint catalogue rather than one copied from Wappalyzer/etc. robots

items.title: 米家空调「冷媒动态调节」等4项技术获评「国际领先」

excerpt_i18n.en: This year's college entrance exam season, Xiaomi's home appliances also faced a special "test"—presenting four core technologies for evaluation by an authoritative industry expert committee. Recently, the China Refrigeration Society and the China Energy Conservation Association jointly organized the Xiaomi Home Appliances Series Technology Achievement Appraisal Meeting in Wuhan, Hubei. To date, Xiaomi's home appliances have accumulated 20 key technologies certified as "internationally leading," which have been successively integrated into various flagship products: the Strong Wind Pro series features 9 technologies, the Top Outlet Pro series 9, and the central air conditioning series 6, delivering users a more comfortable, intelligent, and energy-efficient experience. Strong Wind Pro Series｜Dynamic refrigerant regulation + full-temperature-range wide-frequency high-efficiency control: Rapid cooling and heating, precise temperature control, and comprehensive energy savings. Many users face these issues: returning home in midsummer to find the air conditioner slow to cool down; experiencing fluctuating room temperatures during nighttime sleep; and seeing the air conditioner become a major energy drain on monthly electricity bills. Xiaomi's dynamic refrigerant regulation technology addresses this by dynamically and intelligently adjusting the system's refrigerant volume based on actual demand—increasing refrigerant supply for rapid cooling and heating, and reducing it when the room temperature stabilizes.

title_i18n.es: El proveedor australiano de servicios en la nube de IA, Sharon AI, ha alcanzado un acuerdo de colaboración de seis años con NVIDIA.

excerpt_i18n.zh: 6月12日，澳大利亚人工智能云服务提供商Sharon AI宣布与英伟达签署为期六年的AI基础设施算力合作协议。根据协议，双方将在澳大利亚新增72兆瓦（MW）数据中心容量，并部署英伟达DSX AI Factory架构，未来可扩展至4万块Grace Blackwell GB300 GPU，以满足AI初创企业、商业客户及高校研究机构不断增长的算力需求。（界面）
excerpt_i18n.en: On June 12, Australian AI cloud service provider Sharon AI announced a six-year AI infrastructure computing power cooperation agreement with NVIDIA. Under the agreement, the two parties will add 72 megawatts (MW) of data center capacity in Australia and deploy NVIDIA's DSX AI Factory architecture, which can be expanded to 40,000 Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs in the future to meet the growing computing power demands of AI startups, commercial clients, and university research institutions. (Interface)
excerpt_i18n.es: El 12 de junio, el proveedor australiano de servicios en la nube de inteligencia artificial Sharon AI anunció la firma de un acuerdo de cooperación en capacidad de cómputo de infraestructura de IA con Nvidia por seis años. Según el acuerdo, ambas partes añadirán 72 megavatios (MW) de capacidad de centro de datos en Australia y desplegarán la arquitectura DSX AI Factory de Nvidia, que podrá ampliarse en el futuro hasta 40.000 GPU Grace Blackwell GB300, para satisfacer la creciente demanda de capacidad de cómputo de startups de IA, clientes comerciales e instituciones de investigación universitarias. (Jiemian)
